item.title: #3625969: Twig's 3.30 TypeError: Twig\Runtime\EscaperRuntime::escape(): Argument #4 ($autoescape) must be of type bool, null given
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 10.6.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +72/−14 · php +72/−14
  • Diff: b4659e2
  • Discussion: #3625969 · 21 contributors · 53 comments
  • Followers: 55

Summary

Twig 3.30 changed how its escape/e filter compiles, and Drupal's mechanism for swapping in its own MarkupInterface-aware escaping broke as a result: every templated page threw a TypeError and produced a white screen of death. This fix restores compatibility so sites can run Drupal with Twig 3.30 (or Twig 3.28/3.29) without the crash. Anyone who had pinned twig/twig to an older version as a workaround can lift that pin once they update to a core release containing this fix.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Twig 3.30 introduced a dedicated EscapeFilter node that compiles directly to $this->escaper->escape(...). Drupal's TwigNodeVisitor::leaveNode() previously handled escape/e filters by swapping the compiled node's callable to Drupal's own drupal_escape filter, but leaving Twig's own EscapeFilter node in place to build the call. Twig 3.30 still emitted the direct escaper->escape() call, but built its arguments for drupal_escape (which needs the environment as its first parameter), so $this->env was inserted as an extra leading argument, every other argument shifted over, and null (the charset) ended up in the $autoescape boolean slot.

Rather than swapping the callable on Twig's own escape node at parse time, TwigExtension::getFilters() now registers Drupal's escapeFilter method directly under the names escape and e (in addition to drupal_escape), reusing a shared $escape_options array. Because Twig loads Drupal's extension after its own EscaperExtension, and later-registered filters of the same name win, Twig's built-in escape node/filter is overridden outright and never compiled, so the argument-shifting bug can't occur regardless of Twig version. A new TwigExtension::escapeFilterIsSafe() static method replaces the previous reliance on Twig's internal twig_escape_filter_is_safe helper as the is_safe_callback. TwigNodeVisitor::leaveNode() was simplified accordingly: it no longer swaps the node's callable, it just checks whether the filter name is escape, e, or drupal_escape to set $this->skipRenderVarFunction. A new testEscapeFilterOverride() test in TwigExtensionTest asserts that both explicit (|escape, |e) and automatic escaping compile to Drupal's own escapeFilter method.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 25, 2026
  • Committed: September 25, 2026

Key contributors

  • gábor hojtsy (Acquia)
  • godotislate
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • f0ns (Webhaven)
  • ykhalid

Collaboration

The fix converged quickly through parallel experimentation: gáborhojtsy opened an initial MR (!17242) that kept the parse-time callable-swap approach but built a fresh FilterExpression node, based on a suggestion from the upstream Twig issue thread. longwave then proposed an alternative in MR !17244, overriding the escape/e filter definitions themselves instead of touching the node visitor's callable-swap logic, noting it "should be more performant". catch committed longwave's MR (!17244) to main and 12.0.x, commenting "Agreed with taking this out of runtime." godotislate and f0ns independently verified both MRs against real Twig 3.28/3.30 behavior (f0ns compared escaping output across several template constructs on a live 11.4.7 site) before the backports to 11.x, 11.4.x and 10.6.x followed.</collaboration> <parameter name="ai_disclosures">[{"uid": 4166, "username": "gábor hojtsy", "tool": "Opus", "cid": 16784606}, {"uid": 205645, "username": "phenaproxima", "tool": "Opus", "cid": 16784631}, {"uid": 246492, "username": "longwave", "tool": "Claude Opus 5.5", "cid": 16784698}]

item.title: #3581349: Remove Syndicate block config
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +158/−0 · php +96 · yml +62
  • Diff: be4d779
  • Discussion: #3581349 · 5 contributors · 21 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

The Syndicate block (the RSS feed icon block) was deprecated in Drupal 11.2 with no replacement and its plugin code was removed ahead of Drupal 12. That left orphaned block.block.* configuration on any site that still had the block placed. Running database updates to Drupal 12.0.0 now automatically deletes that leftover block configuration, in any theme, not just Olivero where the block originally lived.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New block_post_update_remove_syndicate_blocks() post update deletes any block.block.* configuration using the removed node_syndicate_block plugin whose settings.provider is node, in any theme.

Technical details

The fix adds block_post_update_remove_syndicate_blocks() in core/modules/block/block.post_update.php, which loads all block config entities with plugin set to node_syndicate_block and settings.provider set to node, and deletes them. Restricting the match to settings.provider: node (rather than just the plugin ID) means a block config entity that a contrib or custom module has taken over, for example by changing its provider, such as the stark_custom_syndicate fixture with provider: custom_syndicate, is left alone.

Test coverage was added in BlockRemoveSyndicateBlocksUpdateTest, using new fixtures (block.block.olivero_syndicate.yml, block.block.stark_syndicate.yml, block.block.stark_custom_syndicate.yml) loaded via a new syndicate-block-config.php update fixture script, verifying that Syndicate blocks in both Olivero and Stark are removed while the provider-overridden block and unrelated blocks survive the update. The related issue #3518990 originally deprecated the SyndicateBlock plugin before its removal in core.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 25, 2026
  • Committed: September 24, 2026 (6 months later)

Key contributors

  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • xjm (Zoocha)
  • gábor hojtsy (Acquia)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

catch traced the history of the change (deprecation in #3518990, code removal in #3571623) and laid out the tradeoff: leave the zombie config with a release note telling sites to check for it, or add an update to delete it outright, at the risk that some site is still relying on it. Gábor Hojtsy reasoned that because the code removal had only ever landed on the main branch and never in a released version, no site could yet have taken ownership of the config by reimplementing the plugin, which made it safe to delete now; he then opened the merge request implementing the deletion. xjm pushed for a more discoverable change record rather than relying on release notes alone, and catch added one before the fix was committed.

item.title: #3621277: Update JavaScript dependencies for 12.0.0-beta1
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 17 files, +1762/−1628 · lock +1710/−1575 · json +25/−25 · js +17/−18 · yml +9/−9 · map +1/−1
  • Diff: 581f9a5
  • Discussion: #3621277 · 7 contributors · 43 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 7 contributors

Summary

Ahead of Drupal 12.0.0-beta1, core's bundled JavaScript build and lint tooling dependencies were refreshed to their latest versions (Yarn packages such as webpack, terser, jsdom, chokidar, glob, cspell, prettier, stylelint, and vendored front-end libraries like floating-ui, sortablejs, tabbable and tua-body-scroll-lock). This is mostly an internal maintenance update with no effect on site configuration or content, but it does include one change that can affect custom JavaScript: the bundled transliteration library used for generating machine names now exposes its transliterate function differently, so code that referenced the old global must be updated.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The bundled transliteration vendor library (2.3.5 to 2.6.1) now exposes a transliteration object instead of a transliterate global function; core/misc/machine-name.js was updated to call transliteration.transliterate.

Technical details

The update was produced largely by running yarn upgrade-interactive and yarn vendor-update and regenerating derived build artifacts. The one behavior-relevant change: the transliteration npm package (2.3.5 to 2.6.1) changed its browser bundle from a transliterate global function to a transliteration object, so core/misc/machine-name.js now calls transliteration.transliterate(...) instead of transliterate(...), and the ESLint globals list in eslint.config.mjs was updated to declare transliteration instead of transliterate.

Several riskier or larger bumps found during the upgrade were deliberately deferred to follow-up issues to keep this change reviewable: ESLint 10 (blocked on eslint-plugin-import lacking a compatible release, tracked in #3625189), postcss/postcss-import (tracked in #3625308, since their whitespace-handling change would have regenerated 121 compiled CSS files), and eslint-plugin-yml 3.x (tracked in #3625576). The stylelint-config-standard bump to 40.0.0 enables the property-no-deprecated rule, which flags 74 existing uses of deprecated CSS properties (page-break-*, word-wrap, clip) in core themes; rather than fixing those here, the rule was set to null in .stylelintrc.json until #3625187 addresses them. eslint-plugin-no-jquery was bumped to 6.0.0, which supports flat ESLint config natively, so the fixupPluginRules() wrapper and the now-unused @eslint/compat dependency were removed from eslint.config.mjs. Vendored copies of @floating-ui/dom, sortablejs, tabbable and tua-body-scroll-lock under core/assets/vendor were regenerated, and the CKEditor 5 plugin builds were regenerated due to newer webpack/terser output.

Upgrade

Custom or contrib JavaScript that relies on the transliterate global provided by core's core/transliteration library must update the call site:

// Before
transliterate(source, options);

// After
transliteration.transliterate(source, options);

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 7, 2026
  • Committed: September 24, 2026 (17 days later)

Key contributors

  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • xjm (Zoocha)
  • gábor hojtsy (Acquia)
  • godotislate
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

Gábor Hojtsy prepared the dependency update and, in comment #16778296, explained the reasoning behind each package bump after using an LLM to help work out the causes of the changes. Longwave reviewed the resulting merge request and pushed back on relying on an LLM's explanation instead of reading each major version's own changelog for breaking changes, specifically pointing out that eslint-plugin-yml's default config reference had changed. That review led to splitting the change into a smaller, easier-to-review update: the postcss/postcss-import bump (and its resulting whitespace-only CSS regeneration) was moved to #3625308, the eslint-plugin-yml bump was reverted and deferred to #3625576, and ESLint 10 was deferred to #3625189, leaving only the lower-risk bumps (stylelint, transliteration, eslint-plugin-no-jquery, and the rest) to land here.

item.title: #3095257: Option for _none is removed once a field has a value and can cause accidental data corruption
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 11.4.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +129/−20 · php +129/−20
  • Diff: b50fd00
  • Discussion: #3095257 · 20 contributors · 124 comments
  • Followers: 27

Summary

Required entity reference fields using the "Select list" widget (for example a required taxonomy term reference) could silently corrupt data. If the referenced entity was deleted, or became inaccessible to the current user, the widget's usual "- Select a value -" placeholder disappeared and the select box defaulted to the first available option instead. Editors who saved the form without noticing would overwrite the field with an unintended value. Now, when a required single-value select has no valid selection, the widget adds a "- Select a value -" option and forces the editor to explicitly pick a real value before the form can be saved, rather than defaulting to an arbitrary option.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The bug was in OptionsSelectWidget::getEmptyLabel(), which decided whether to show a placeholder option based solely on $this->has_value (whether the field item list originally had a value), not on whether that value was still present among the currently available options. When a referenced entity was deleted or became inaccessible, has_value remained TRUE even though the resulting default value was empty, so no placeholder was added and the browser's <select> fell back to auto-selecting its first <option>.

The fix moves the decision into OptionsSelectWidget::formElement(): it computes $options and $selected directly, determines whether the field will render as a multiple select (accounting for the case where a multi-value field collapses to a single select because only one option remains), and if the field is required, not multiple, and $selected is empty, prepends a synthetic _none option labeled "- Select a value -" so the browser has an explicit non-answer to fall back to instead of the first real option. getEmptyLabel() itself is simplified to only return '- None -' for non-required fields (used elsewhere for the optional case) and no longer inspects has_value at all.

The fix intentionally preserves existing auto-select behavior for multi-value (multiple-select) widgets and for the case where a required field has exactly one available option and no prior value (for example when creating a new entity), since changing that was judged out of scope; a UX warning for the "value became unavailable" case was deferred to follow-up #3623828, and a broader entity-reference-on-delete data integrity concern was noted for a separate follow-up issue.</technical> <parameter name="collaboration">The issue took years to land: an initial patch approach (has_value recalculation) drew review from alexpott and catch pointing out it didn't correctly account for hook_options_list_alter() and contrib widgets reusing getEmptyLabel(), and was flagged as a "hard problem" by the Bug Smash Initiative. It was picked up again by mstrelan (who recorded a reproduction screencast) and smustgrave, who wrote the final MR. During final review alexpott identified that an early version of the fix regressed the existing behavior of auto-selecting the sole option on a required field with only one choice, and after discussion the MR was adjusted to run the empty-option logic based on the actual resolved $options and multiple state so both single- and multi-select configurations, including a multi-value field collapsing to a single select, behave consistently. acbramley's final review caught a missing return in getEmptyLabel() before it was marked RTBC and committed by alexpott.</collaboration> <parameter name="ai_disclosures">[{"uid": 3252890, "username": "smustgrave", "tool": "", "cid": 16766733}]

item.title: #3037054: Deprecate drupal_static_reset() and drupal_static()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 12 files, +76/−10 · php +76/−10
  • Diff: 903f52d
  • Discussion: #3037054 · 8 contributors · 30 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 8 contributors

Summary

The long-standing procedural helpers drupal_static() and drupal_static_reset(), used to define reset-able static variables inside functions, are now formally deprecated and will be removed in Drupal 13.0.0. Sites and modules that still call these functions directly will start seeing deprecation notices and should switch to the memory cache backend instead. Core's own remaining internal callers (in batch processing, CSS optimization, machine name form validation, comment search indexing, and admin theme settings overrides) have already been converted to use \Drupal::cache('memory') directly.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: drupal_static() and drupal_static_reset() are deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and removed in drupal:13.0.0; use \Drupal::cache('memory')->get(), ->set(), and ->delete() instead.

Technical details

The deprecation notices are added directly inside drupal_static() and drupal_static_reset() in core/includes/bootstrap.inc. Because both functions can legitimately be called many times per request (and core itself still needs to call drupal_static_reset() globally to flush all statics in a few places), a naive @trigger_error() on every call would spam PHPUnit's deprecation handling and logs. To avoid that, each function first checks a per-$name marker in \Drupal::cache('memory'); the deprecation is triggered only the first time a given $name is seen in the request, then the marker cache entry suppresses further triggers for that name.

A special sentinel value, 'clear_all_skip_deprecation', was introduced so that core's own "reset every static" call sites (drupal_flush_all_caches(), KernelTestBase::tearDown(), and FunctionalTestSetupTrait::tearDown()) can still clear all statics via drupal_static_reset() without triggering the deprecation on themselves; these call sites are marked with // @phpstan-ignore function.deprecated.

Remaining core call sites that used drupal_static() as a lightweight per-request cache (_batch_needs_update() in core/includes/batch.inc, FormElementBase/MachineName::getTransliterationLanguageOverrides(), CommentHooks::nodeUpdateIndex(), and Settings::userOverrideEnabled() in core/themes/default_admin) were rewritten to read and write \Drupal::cache('memory') directly, matching the pattern already used elsewhere for drupal_static_reset() replacements like options.allowed_values. ResettableStaticTest was updated with #[IgnoreDeprecations] and expectUserDeprecationMessage() assertions to cover the new deprecation paths.

Upgrade

Replace direct calls to drupal_static() and drupal_static_reset() with the memory cache backend. For example, code that previously did:

$overrides = &drupal_static(__CLASS__ . '_' . __METHOD__, []);

should become:

$cid = __CLASS__ . '_' . __METHOD__;
$cached = \Drupal::cache('memory')->get($cid);
$overrides = $cached->data ?? [];
// ... after computing/updating $overrides:
\Drupal::cache('memory')->set($cid, $overrides);

And a reset call like:

drupal_static_reset('my_cache_id');

becomes:

\Drupal::cache('memory')->delete('my_cache_id');

Calling drupal_static_reset() with no arguments (to reset all statics) is also deprecated; there is no direct drop-in replacement for clearing every memory cache entry at once, so only internal core bootstrap code retains this ability via the 'clear_all_skip_deprecation' sentinel.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 2, 2019
  • Committed: September 24, 2026 (7 years later)

Key contributors

  • mile23
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • daffie (Finalist)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

The issue sat open for over seven years. catch noted on commit that using a memory cache for the handful of remaining internal callers made it possible to finally start warning contrib about drupal_static()'s eventual removal, calling it "good to be able to commit this one seven years (!) after it was opened." nicxvan proposed the concrete approach that unblocked the issue: introducing the clear_all (later clear_all_skip_deprecation) sentinel so the few call sites that must reset all statics globally could keep doing so without triggering the deprecation, while all other calls would warn. feuerwagen thanked claudiu.cristea specifically for having "chipped away at this for (8+!) years."

item.title: #3067979: Exclude test files from release packages
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +52/−40 · gitattributes +35/−32 · php +17/−8
  • Diff: b8367ad
  • Discussion: #3067979 · 50 contributors · 173 comments
  • Followers: 78

Summary

Starting with Drupal 12 (main), the tests directory under Drupal core is excluded from the packages that most sites actually download: the Composer "dist" zip and the release tarballs built by drupal.org. This shrinks the on-disk footprint of a typical Drupal installation (tests accounted for a large share of core's total file count) and removes test code, which the issue's participants noted has occasionally been a source of security concerns, from production deployments. Nothing changes for anyone working from a git checkout of core, including core contributors and the testbot. Sites and projects that need to run tests which rely on core's test base classes or core-only test modules (for example when testing custom or contributed code against core, or applying patches that touch test files) need to install drupal/core from source instead of from the default dist package.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: Projects that run automated tests extending core test base classes (e.g. KernelTestBase, WebDriverTestBase) or depending on core test-only modules must install drupal/core from source (e.g. composer install --prefer-source for that package) since dist packages/tarballs no longer ship core/tests.

Technical details

The mechanism is a new core/.gitattributes file with a tests export-ignore (and .gitattributes export-ignore) directive. Drupal.org's packaging pipeline builds releases with git-archive, which honors export-ignore, so the entire core/tests directory is dropped from both the packaged tarball and the Composer dist zip without any change to the packaging scripts themselves.

This landed in three steps. The first commit (5341dd83) tried a fine-grained approach, excluding most test paths but carving out exceptions such as modules/*/tests/src/ and profiles/tests/testing/ so that base test classes contrib relies on (like WebDriverTestBase) would survive in dist packages. That broke contrib CI within hours because those base classes still depend on test-only helper modules (js_testing_ajax_request_test, js_testing_log_test, css_disable_transitions_test, entity_test, performance_test, etc.) that lived in the excluded paths, so it was reverted (34b130bd). After discussion of the maintenance burden of an ever-growing exceptions list versus the simplicity of --prefer-source, the maintainers landed a much simpler final version (b8367add): core/.gitattributes excludes the entire tests directory, with no carve-outs, on the understanding that anyone needing core's test infrastructure installs drupal/core from source.

Because Package Manager's own build tests assemble a Composer project from the checked-out core codebase, its TemplateProjectTestBase::createTestProject() now explicitly mirrors the package_manager module's own test modules into the built test project, since those modules are no longer present when core is installed as a dist package.

Follow-up work was split out rather than handled here: a gitlab_templates change to default CI to --prefer-source for drupal/core, plus separate issues #3625050 (documenting composer-patches usage without patching tests) and #3625358 (deciding what to do with run-tests.sh and similar dev scripts in dist builds, which currently fail without the excluded test code).</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">If your project or CI pipeline runs tests that depend on Drupal core's test base classes, traits, or test-only modules (for example Drupal\Tests\...\KernelTestBase, WebDriverTestBase, or fixture/test modules under core/tests or core/modules/*/tests), install drupal/core from source rather than from dist, for instance:

composer install --prefer-source

or, to target only core:

composer config --global preferred-install.drupal/core source

Patches that modify files under any tests directory will also fail to apply against a dist install of core; see #3625050 for guidance on stripping test-only changes from patches.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: July 15, 2019
  • First commit: August 25, 2026 (7 years later)
  • Last commit: September 23, 2026 (29 days and 3 commits later)

Key contributors

  • traviscarden (Acquia)
  • danepowell (Acquia)
  • effulgentsia (Acquia)
  • drumm (Drupal Association)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • webchick (Acquia)
  • Mixologic (Drupal Association)
  • mile23
  • greggles (Morris Animal Foundation)
  • adamps (AlbanyWeb)
  • mglaman (Centarro)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • xjm (Zoocha)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • amateescu
  • acbramley (PreviousNext)
  • pameeela (Technocrat)
  • cmlara (DM13 Security LLC)
  • mstrelan
  • mably (Bordeaux Metropole)
  • spiderman (Consensus Enterprises)
  • star-szr (Consensus Enterprises)

Collaboration

The initial fine-grained .gitattributes (5341dd83) shipped with exceptions meant to keep contrib-usable base test classes available, but marcelovani reported within hours that it broke FunctionalJavascript tests across core and contrib because WebDriverTestBase installs test-only helper modules that had been excluded; catch reverted it the same day. mstrelan separately pushed back on an AI-generated bug report in the thread, asking contributors to "understand the output and communicate with us humans with human language." Following the revert, spiderman and star-szr did hands-on investigation with gitlab-ci-local to reproduce the contrib CI failures and test the --prefer-source workaround end to end, and cmlara pressed for the exceptions-based approach to be validated more rigorously (tracing every base class's module and file dependencies) rather than just checked visually. That investigation, combined with longwave's finding that the exceptions list would need to keep growing, led catch and longwave to abandon the fine-grained exclusions and land the simple, exception-free version instead.</collaboration> <ai_disclosures">[]</ai_disclosures> </invoke>

item.title: #3532930: Make Drupal\Core\Database\Database type strict and PHPStan L10 compliant
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +271/−173 · php +271/−173
  • Diff: 3a8ca18
  • Discussion: #3532930 · 8 contributors · 45 comments
  • Followers: 11
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 8 contributors

Summary

The Drupal\Core\Database\Database class, along with Connection::setKey()/setTarget() and Log::__construct(), has been made type strict and fully documented for PHPStan's strictest level. Connection keys and targets (the identifiers used to select which database to talk to, e.g. 'default') have always been documented as strings, but the code silently accepted integers too. That silent acceptance is now deprecated: passing an integer key or target still works today but triggers a deprecation notice and will throw a TypeError once removed in Drupal 13. Sites and contributed modules that pass integers as database keys or targets (for example in multi-database setups) should switch to strings.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Drupal\Core\Database\Database's static methods now declare native string|int parameter types and return types (e.g. getConnection(string|int $target = 'default', string|int|null $key = NULL): Connection) instead of being untyped, and the class itself now uses declare(strict_types=1).
  • Deprecation: Passing a non-string value as the database connection $key or $target to Drupal\Core\Database\Database methods (getConnection(), addConnectionInfo(), startLog(), getLog(), setActiveConnection(), getConnectionInfo(), renameConnection(), removeConnection(), openConnection(), closeConnection(), ignoreTarget(), getConnectionInfoAsUrl()), to Connection::setKey()/setTarget(), or to Log::__construct() is deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and is removed from drupal:13.0.0.

Technical details

The class gained declare(strict_types=1); and PHPStan-level-10-compliant documentation, including new @phpstan-type array shapes (UnprocessedConnectionInfoArray, ConnectionInfoArray in Database.php, DatabaseLogEntry in Log.php) that describe the connection-info and query-log array structures instead of relying on array alone. All previously-untyped static methods (startLog(), getLog(), getConnection(), setActiveConnection(), parseConnectionInfo(), addConnectionInfo(), getConnectionInfo(), getAllConnectionInfo(), setMultipleConnectionInfo(), renameConnection(), removeConnection(), openConnection(), closeConnection(), ignoreTarget(), getConnectionInfoAsUrl()) now declare native parameter and return types, mostly string|int for keys/targets to preserve backward compatibility, with a @trigger_error() deprecation added wherever an int is passed instead of the documented string. Internally, values are cast with (string) before being handed to Connection::setTarget()/setKey() or Log's constructor, since those now also deprecate non-string input under the stricter typing PHPStan otherwise enforces across the call chain.

parseConnectionInfo() was reworked to build a fresh $connection_info array (asserting namespace/autoload end up set) rather than mutating the incoming $info in place, which also let outdated Drupal 8 backward-compatibility test cases for the old Drupal\Driver\Database\* namespace layout (removed back in #3294695) be dropped from SettingsTest. A follow-up, #3533038, proposes replacing the long connection-info array shape with a ConnectionParameters value object, but was postponed in favor of this narrower type-strictness pass. item.title: #3612965: Allow Guzzle 8 in Drupal 11
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +131/−338 · php +87/−73 · lock +42/−257 · json +2/−8
  • Diff: 9df766b
  • Discussion: #3612965 · 5 contributors · 23 comments
  • Followers: 9
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Drupal core's composer.json now allows sites to install either Guzzle 7 or Guzzle 8 as the underlying HTTP client library, even though Drupal 11 itself continues to ship and be tested with Guzzle 7 by default. This backports the Guzzle 8 compatibility work originally done for Drupal 12 in #3612544, giving Drupal 11 site owners the option to move to Guzzle 8 in case Guzzle 7 reaches end of life before Drupal 11 does.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: guzzlehttp/guzzle constraint widened from ^7.10 to ^7.10 || ^8.0 (and guzzlehttp/psr7 to ^2.8.0 || ^3.0); Drupal 11 still ships and is tested with Guzzle 7 (bumped to 7.15.5) by default.

Technical details

The version constraints for guzzlehttp/guzzle and guzzlehttp/psr7 in core's composer.json were widened to ^7.10 || ^8.0 and ^2.8.0 || ^3.0 respectively, but composer.lock keeps the actually-installed version on Guzzle 7 (bumped to 7.15.5) rather than jumping to Guzzle 8, so nothing changes for sites that don't touch their own lock file.

To make Drupal's own code and test suite tolerate whichever version a site chooses, several compatibility shims were added: FileCookieJarShim now only defines its hardened backport of GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar when GuzzleHttp\ClientInterface::MAJOR_VERSION < 8, since Guzzle 8 ships that hardening natively, and its test skips itself under Guzzle 8. DrupalTestBrowser::doRequest() catches GuzzleHttp\Exception\BadResponseException instead of RequestException to match Guzzle 8's exception hierarchy. BrowserTestBase::loginHttps() falls back to parsing the raw Set-Cookie header via SetCookie::fromString() because Guzzle 8 no longer stores secure cookies received over the test's insecure HTTPS mock connection in its CookieJar. Kernel-test HTTP handler callables must now return a GuzzleHttp\Promise\PromiseInterface (via GuzzleHttp\Promise\Create::promiseFor()) instead of a bare Response, since Guzzle 8 changed the handler signature to ($request, array $options). A couple of assertions on Guzzle exception message text in UpdateAdvisoriesTest and UpdateFetcherTest were loosened to accept either the Guzzle 7 or Guzzle 8 message formatting. The php-http/guzzle7-adapter dev dependency was dropped.

Upgrade

No action is required for existing sites: Drupal 11 continues to lock to Guzzle 7 by default. Sites or modules that want to move to Guzzle 8 can now do so, since core's constraint permits it:

"guzzlehttp/guzzle": "^7.10 || ^8.0"

Run composer require guzzlehttp/guzzle:^8.0 to opt in. Code that directly catches GuzzleHttp\Exception\RequestException and expects it to cover bad HTTP responses should be aware Guzzle 8 uses GuzzleHttp\Exception\BadResponseException for that case.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: July 24, 2026
  • Committed: September 16, 2026 (1 month and 3 commits later)

Key contributors

  • godotislate
  • daffie (Finalist)

Collaboration

The initial commit landed the wrong merge request (MR 16839, which fully bumped composer.lock to Guzzle 8) instead of the intended MR 17094, which kept composer.lock on Guzzle 7 while allowing Guzzle 8. godotislate flagged the mistake in comment #16772202, and catch confirmed and corrected it: "Yes... got my tabs mixed up. Reverted the wrong MR, and committed the right one this time." godotislate also did the work of resolving merge conflicts and fixing test failures on the correct MR, tracing one remaining failure to an unrelated upstream issue (#3182064).

Summary

The Toolbar module, the classic black admin bar shown across the top of the page for users with access, has been removed from Drupal core entirely. It had already been deprecated (#3560123) since the Navigation module became the default admin toolbar. Sites that still rely on Toolbar (for example those that opted out of Navigation) need to install the Toolbar contrib module before updating, or migrate to Navigation.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: Sites with the toolbar module enabled will get an update-path error naming it as a removed core module (SystemRequirements::DRUPAL_CORE_REMOVED_MODULE_LIST) until it is uninstalled or replaced by the contrib version.

Technical details

The commit deletes core/modules/toolbar in its entirety: the module's PHP (ToolbarHooks, ToolbarController, Element/Toolbar, Element/ToolbarItem, link builders for user/announcements/workspaces, etc.), its Twig templates, libraries, permissions, routing, breakpoints, all CSS/PCSS/SVG assets, the toolbar_test and toolbar_disable_user_toolbar test support modules, and the full functional/unit/Nightwatch test suites, 127 files and roughly 11,800 lines in total.

Outside the module directory, the change is minimal since Toolbar's responsibilities had already been migrated to the Navigation module in prior issues (including #3618746, which moved Toolbar-only integration code out of the User, Contextual, and Announcements Feed modules). The only functional addition is in SystemRequirements::DRUPAL_CORE_REMOVED_MODULE_LIST, where 'toolbar' => 'Toolbar' is added so update.php flags any site that still has the module enabled. core/.phpstan-baseline.php and core/MAINTAINERS.txt are trimmed of now-dead references.

Upgrade

If a site still has the toolbar module enabled, running database updates will fail with a removed-module error until the module is uninstalled or replaced. To keep the classic admin bar, install the contrib Toolbar module before updating:

composer require drupal/toolbar

Otherwise, use the core Navigation module, which is enabled by default and replaces Toolbar's functionality.

item.title: #2876298: Remove scaffolded csslint and eslint config
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 18 files, +0/−88 · md +0/−6 · json +0/−24 · txt +0/−1 · php +0/−12 · csslintrc +0/−37 · eslintignore +0/−8
  • Discussion: #2876298 · 16 contributors · 47 comments
  • Followers: 28
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 16 contributors

Summary

Drupal no longer scaffolds a .csslintrc, .eslintignore, or .eslintrc.json file into the root of every site built from drupal/core-composer-scaffold. CSSLint was replaced by stylelint back in 2017 (#2865971) and is considered dead, and the scaffolded ESLint config stopped working once core moved to ESLint v9 with a new config format (#3440225). Since using these tools requires manually installing ESLint/CSSLint plus the matching plugins anyway, and most real sites already keep their own lint configuration at the theme or repository root, core stops shipping these unused defaults into every install. This is a disruptive change targeted at Drupal 12.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Composer scaffold no longer copies .csslintrc, .eslintignore, or .eslintrc.json into the web root of new or updated Drupal sites.

Technical details

The fix removes the [web-root]/.csslintrc, [web-root]/.eslintignore, and [web-root]/.eslintrc.json entries from the drupal-scaffold file-mapping in core/composer.json (and the corresponding fixture composer.json files used by drupal-composer-scaffold tests), and deletes the source files themselves from assets/scaffold/files/ (csslintrc, eslintignore, eslintrc.json). Test fixtures and expectations across the scaffold plugin's test suite (e.g. ManageGitIgnoreTest, drush-style scaffold listing output) were updated to no longer expect these files to be copied or linked.

Core's own internal .eslintrc.json and .stylelintrc.json inside core/ are untouched. Only the copies that composer-scaffold writes out to the site's web root are removed, so core's own lint tooling and CI keep working; it is only external sites and themes that lose the auto-provisioned copy.

Upgrade

Sites that want to keep linting against core's rules must now do so manually, since the scaffolded copy is gone. Before this change, the scaffolded .eslintrc.json simply contained:

{
  "extends": "./core/.eslintrc.json"
}

Sites relying on this can recreate that file themselves (adjusting the relative path to core/.eslintrc.json if their web root differs), or point their own lint configuration directly at core's core/.eslintrc.json / core/.stylelintrc.json. There is no scaffolded .csslintrc replacement, since CSSLint itself is obsolete; use stylelint instead.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 6, 2017

Key contributors

  • alexpott (Chapter Three (acquired by Kanopi Studios))
  • xjm (Acquia)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • nod_ (Très Bien Tech)
  • godotislate
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

The main open question was whether this would break contrib CI. alexpott flagged that #3559584, the companion issue in the gitlab_templates project to move these linting scaffold files to the assets folder, was still unresolved when the MR was ready. fjgarlin had already opened that issue ahead of time to handle the contrib-CI side. neclimdul pushed on the practical question of how custom themes/sites are meant to keep following core's lint rules once the scaffolded copies disappear, given years of the scaffolded ESLint config being broken while waiting on #3440225; longwave clarified that core's own .eslintrc.json/.stylelintrc.json inside core/ are unaffected and can still be referenced directly, though making that reuse convenient is left to a separate issue.

item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 19 files, +38/−0 · php +36 · yml +2
  • Diff: b11f868

  • Followers: 8

Summary

The core Toolbar module (the admin toolbar shown at the top of the page for authenticated users with access) is now officially deprecated. This follows the policy decision in #3476882 to move Toolbar out of core and into a contributed project. Sites that currently use Toolbar will start seeing deprecation notices, and should begin planning to switch to a contributed replacement before Toolbar is eventually removed from Drupal core. The module still works as before; only its lifecycle status has changed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: The toolbar module is now marked lifecycle: deprecated in its .info.yml, per the approved plan to move it to a contributed project; sites using it will see deprecation notices and should plan to migrate before it is removed from core.

Technical details

The change adds lifecycle: deprecated and lifecycle_link: https://www.drupal.org/node/3223395#s-toolbar to core/modules/toolbar/toolbar.info.yml, which is how Drupal core's extension lifecycle system flags a module as deprecated (surfacing warnings on the modules page and via hook_deprecation_message-style runtime notices per the extension deprecation policy). Every functional, unit, and JavaScript test under core/modules/toolbar/tests also received the #[IgnoreDeprecations] PHPUnit attribute, so the tests keep passing despite the module now being flagged as deprecated, without needing to fix or suppress each individual deprecation notice.

This is one step in the broader deprecation effort tracked in the meta issue for the Toolbar removal; the remaining cleanup of Toolbar-only code still embedded in other core modules (Announcement, User, Contextual, Workspaces) is handled separately in #3618746.

Upgrade

Sites and contributed/custom modules that depend on the core toolbar module should start planning a migration to a contributed replacement. No code changes are required yet: the module's functionality is unchanged, but it now reports as deprecated:

# core/modules/toolbar/toolbar.info.yml
lifecycle: deprecated
lifecycle_link: https://www.drupal.org/node/3223395#s-toolbar
